notes:
• D&D 5e sheet tabs as a labeled row: a new setting, off by default, lays the tabs of the system's character, NPC and vehicle sheets in a row across the sheet, each with its name beside its icon, instead of the icons hung down its side. It is the layout Carolingian UI offers, for tables that don't run it. The tabs are still the system's own, in its colors, and the rest of the sheet is left alone; only the character's ability scores move, to sit just under the row. A row too long for a narrow sheet scrolls with the mouse wheel or the arrow at its end. Where Carolingian UI's own option is on, the HUD leaves the tabs to it.
  • Journal size: a new setting sets how large the Journal's book opens, as a share of the room it could take. It is 100% by default, as before; lower it to keep more of the map in view. The Grove look follows it too.
  • Labels that fit: a label too long for its box no longer ends in "…". "Death Saves" was cut to "Death…" on every device. A label now goes onto a second line, and the Roll button beside Death Saves or Dying moves under it when the two don't fit side by side. Single words that were cut short by a few letters on the Vambrace, its looks and the EVA now fit: Perception, Inspiration, Exhaustion, Flat-footed and Nonlethal.
  • The Journal on paper, readable: a run-through of the Journal's default light interface for text that could not be read.
    • Foundry fades the scene controls, the sidebar's tabs, the player list, the scene list and the chat beside a closed sidebar until they are pointed at. Faded over a dark map, the page went to a muddy gray and its ink with it. On the Journal, the Grove and the Crystal they now stop fading while they can still be read. The Journal in the dark and every dark device fade as before.

Full details in the release notes.
